ui.about.title: About the Content
ui.about.lead: Fourteen areas of life: scams, health evidence, social situations, legal rights, emergencies, emotions, focus, family, travel and more. Each volume can be searched, collapsed and skimmed.
ui.about.why.title: How It's Organized
ui.about.why1.title: Separated by life scenario
ui.about.why1.text: Scams, health, relationships, money, cooking, love and growth each have their own volume. Go straight to the one you need instead of reading from cover to cover.
ui.about.why2.title: Every entry stands alone
ui.about.why2.text: Each entry gives one core judgment, a few concrete actions and a memorable line. Order doesn't matter — read the one you find.
ui.about.why3.title: Original links kept
ui.about.why3.text: Every entry ends with a source link. For full arguments, original recipes or current rules, go back to the source.
ui.about.sources.title: Eight guides for reference
ui.about.sources.lead: The thematic sources of each volume are listed below. Copyright and licenses belong to their respective authors.
ui.about.deploy.title: Deploy to your own site
ui.about.deploy.lead: Purely static site, the build product only has the dist directory. Use relative paths and hash routing, so it can be opened normally in the root directory or project subdirectory.
ui.about.deploy.vercel.0: Fork this repository to your own GitHub account.
ui.about.deploy.vercel.1: Select Add New → Project in Vercel to import the warehouse.
ui.about.deploy.vercel.2: Framework selects Vite; the build command is npm run build, and the output directory is dist.
ui.about.deploy.vercel.3: Click Deploy. Each subsequent push will automatically republish.
ui.about.deploy.cloudflare.1: Go to Workers & Pages → Create → Pages → Connect to Git.
ui.about.deploy.cloudflare.2: For the build command, fill in npm run build, and for the output directory, fill in dist.
ui.about.deploy.cloudflare.3: Save and deploy; _redirects of the warehouse root directory are included with the build product.
ui.about.deploy.github.0: Fork this repository and go to Settings → Pages.
ui.about.deploy.github.2: The warehouse already comes with .github/workflows/deploy.yml, so there is no need to create another file.
ui.about.deploy.github.3: Push the code once and publish it to https://<username>.github.io/<warehouse name>/.

guides.name: Anti-fraud and information security
guides.desc: Identify the routine first, and then talk about prevention. Break the scam down into verifiable steps rather than relying on memory to avoid pitfalls.
guides.longDesc: Compiled from "Guide to Prevent Fraud in the World". The core method is not to read through all cases, but to search and verify first when encountering suspicious scenes. The following items are extracted in a unified format of "Judgment → Routine → Action → Emergency", covering high-frequency scams and account security.

principles.title: Search first, then transfer
principles.core: What scams scare is not smart people, but people who are willing to spend three minutes to verify.
actions: Search the link, number, and company name given by the other party separately
Change another channel to confirm with the person involved
Any countdown that is "no waiting after expiration" will be treated as a scam by default
principles.remember: Slow down by three minutes, and you may save three years.

principles.title: First question: What are you talking about?
principles.core: Understand where the money comes from, and then you can understand where the routine is going.
actions: Ask yourself what the other party is after: money, account number, personal information or traffic
Anyone who offers sweeteners first and then invests money should be treated as bait
Pay attention to whether you fall into the high-victim group labels: students, mothers, elderly, job seekers
principles.remember: Look for the chain of interests first, and then look at the words.

principles.title: Part-time job for brushing orders: Those who pay first will not do it
principles.core: Regular part-time job will not let you advance money first.
actions: Reject any prepayment request for "commissions for completing tasks"
Small rebates are the hook, large investments are the knife
Keep chat and transfer records, and call the police immediately if any abnormalities are found
principles.remember: If you want to advance funds, be a liar first.

principles.title: Pretend to be a public prosecutor: hang up and call back yourself
principles.core: A real case handler will not ask you to transfer money over the phone.
actions: Do not continue the conversation during the incoming call. After hanging up, call the official number to verify
Do not download the conference or remote control software specified by the other party
"Secure account", "Capital verification" and "Confidentiality" are dangerous words
principles.remember: The public security organs do not handle cases over the phone, and there are no safe accounts.

principles.title: Account and privacy: guard the entrance
principles.core: The lowest-cost attack path is to get your account directly.
actions: Do not share passwords across different platforms, turn on two-factor verification
Do not enter verification codes on unfamiliar links
Stop showing your ID, tickets and real-time location on social platforms
principles.remember: Verification codes are the last door and will not be given to anyone who asks.

principles.title: Investment and virtual currency: Check the subject first, then talk about income
principles.core: The high-yield narrative is the most common shell of a scam.
actions: Check the platform license and operating entity, do not open an account through a private chat link
"Sure profit", "Insider" and "Bringing orders" are red line words
Stop adding funds immediately when withdrawals are blocked
principles.remember: A project that you don't understand is a project that you will not invest in.

principles.title: After being defrauded: stopping losses takes precedence over pursuing liability
principles.core: The first thing to do is to freeze funds and fix evidence.
actions: Contact the bank or payment platform immediately to report the loss and stop the payment
Save the chat, link, transfer voucher and call the police
Don't believe in the secondary harvest of "paying to help you recover"
principles.remember: Stop the bleeding first, and then settle the account.

guides.name: Cost-effective life
guides.desc: Use the least money, time and energy in exchange for life, money, time and personal freedom.
guides.longDesc: Compiled from "Cost-Effective Life Guide". It is a backlist, not a to-do list. The entries adopt the "cost-benefit-evidence" caliber: settle the accounts first, and then decide whether it is worth doing.

principles.title: Calculate accounts using cost-benefit
principles.core: Whether a piece of advice is worth it depends on what it costs and what it gets in return.
actions: Write down the direct cost, time cost and opportunity cost
Estimate whether the benefit is saving money, time or risk
If the cost is clear but the benefit is vague, try it on a small scale first
principles.remember: Calculate the calculation first, and then make a move.

principles.title: Prioritize plugging the loophole of "Don't die early"
principles.core: The greatest cost-effectiveness is not to sacrifice lifespan and freedom.
actions: Do not drink and drive, do not stay up late and overdraft, and do not participate in high-risk speculation
Regular physical examinations and deal with known abnormal indicators
Stand-up first aid and medication knowledge
principles.remember: Life-saving matters have the highest priority.

principles.title: A negative list is more effective than a positive list
principles.core: Knowing what not to do is often more cost-effective than knowing what to do.
actions: Make your own "Never List": don't borrow money to spend, don't pay for face
Review the pitfalls you have stepped on once every quarter
Write the pitfalls into searchable items, rather than one-time regrets
principles.remember: Make one less mistake, equal to one more profit.

principles.title: Mark the level of evidence for suggestions
principles.core: Not all suggestions are equally worthy of trust.
actions: Distinguish between research conclusions, institutional regulations and personal experience
Pay attention to sample size, effect size and whether there are controls
Write controversies and exceptions into notes instead of omitting them
principles.remember: After grading, you will not be taken away by a "supposedly".

principles.title: Preserve cash flow and health first when you have no money
principles.core: The most expensive decision during the trough is to borrow money for the sake of face.
actions: Calculate the minimum cost of survival first and cut off non-essential expenses
Keep the skills and time that can bring cash
Don't use high-interest debt to solve temporary gaps
principles.remember: Only when you have cash in your hand can you have a choice in your heart.

principles.title: Know the legal red lines in advance
principles.core: There is a price, just step on it once.
actions: Clear the basic rights and obligations in labor, renting, and borrowing
Read the terms before signing, especially liquidated damages and automatic renewal
If you are unsure, check the terms before taking action
principles.remember: Ignorance of the law is not a reason for exemption.

principles.title: Be a backup list, not a task list
principles.core: Guidelines are toolboxes, not checklists.
actions: Only choose one or two of the most relevant ones to try
Record the real feedback after trying
Change if it doesn't work, don't blame yourself
principles.remember: The one that suits you is the best value for money.

guides.name: Human wisdom
guides.desc: From campus to workplace, the methods of getting along are written down into judgments and words that can be used directly.
guides.longDesc: Compiled from "Guide to Human Relations and Sophistication". It is all marked as empirical suggestions, distinguishing between research background, institutional regulations and personal experience. The entries here retain their structure of "Key points of judgment → Specific practices → Examples of speaking skills → Exceptions".

principles.title: Look at the relationship first, then talk about the truth
principles.core: The same sentence has completely different effects in different relationships.
actions: Determine whether the two parties are cooperative, competitive, or purely social
Confirm each other's obligation boundaries and expectations
When unsure, ask first: "What do you need me to do now?"
principles.remember: If the relationship is right, the words are right.

principles.title: Asking for help should be specific, and the response should be timely
principles.core: A vague request for help allows others to answer multiple-choice questions, while a specific request for help requires action questions.
actions: Speak clearly what you want, why, and how much time it will take
Leave room for rejection by the other party
Clearly feedback the results afterwards and take the initiative to repay
principles.remember: Others are helping you, not your ambiguity.

principles.title: At dinners and private occasions, pay attention to information and propriety
principles.core: You cannot take back the information you say.
actions: Don’t disclose privacy, salary and evaluation for others
Don’t use other people’s shortcomings as a topic
Change the topic back to facts or jokes when being questioned
principles.remember: Tighten your mouth, and the road will be longer.

principles.title: Money is the high-voltage line of relationships
principles.core: The moment you borrow money, the relationship starts to count.
actions: Write down the amount and return time for large transactions
Do not guarantee or act as a middleman
If you don’t want to borrow, just say so directly, don’t make vague promises
principles.remember: Talking about money doesn't hurt feelings, only being vague does.

principles.title: In times of conflict, deal with emotions first, then deal with things
principles.core: When people are denied, they cannot listen to any reason.
actions: Restate the other person's feelings first, and then express your own position
Replace "you always" with "What happened this time"
Allow each other to cool down if necessary
principles.remember: Catch the person first, then solve the problem.

principles.title: Boundaries are the prerequisite for long-term relationships
principles.core: Closeness without boundaries will eventually turn into resentment.
actions: Make it clear how far you can help
Provide alternatives to cross-border requests
Allow others to refuse, and allow yourself to refuse
principles.remember: Closeness is maintained by propriety.

principles.title: Words must be able to be used directly
principles.core: Good advice should be reduced to one sentence that can be spoken.
actions: Prepare three statements: initial expression, follow-up questioning, and response and rejection.
Observe the other party’s adjustment signals
Review the actual results after speaking
principles.remember: The method that can be expressed is called a method.

guides.name: Health and Life Extension
guides.desc: Put the research conclusions, effect size and practicality level together, and then decide whether to follow it or not.
guides.longDesc: Compiled from "Programmer's Guide to Extending Life". It is a research ledger that emphasizes that observational correlation does not equal causation, and effect sizes cannot be simply added. The entries here retain the evidence caliber of "Conclusion → Judgment → Action".

principles.title: Distinguish between correlation and causation
principles.core: "Research says A is related to B" does not mean that A causes B.
actions: Look at study design, population, and sample size
Pay attention to effect sizes and confidence intervals, not just "significant"
Don't add up HR/RR from different studies as a definite conclusion
principles.remember: Correlation is not causation, and numbers are not promises.

principles.title: Do the most certain thing first
principles.core: Sleep, exercise, and diet are more worthy of investing first than supplements.
actions: Ensure regular sleep and adequate duration
Maintain a sustainable amount of exercise every week
Reduce ultra-processed foods and sugary drinks
principles.remember: Supplements only make sense if the basics are done right.

principles.title: Diet: less processed, more natural, control the total amount
principles.core: Instead of chasing a certain "superfood", it is better to change the overall structure.
actions: Increase fruits and vegetables, whole grains and nuts
Control red meat and sodium intake
Be skeptical of the single conclusion that "a certain food extends life"
principles.remember: Model is more important than a single product.

principles.title: Write the level of evidence next to the recommendation
principles.core: The credibility of the same recommendation may vary by several levels.
actions: Mark the conclusion as supported, partially supported, or not supported
Record limitations and applicable groups
Separately look at the practical level and the strength of the evidence
principles.remember: Look at the conclusion and how strong it is.

principles.title: Don’t ignore environmental exposure
principles.core: Factors such as air pollution and prolonged sitting are often underestimated.
actions: Pay attention to air quality and reduce exposure during periods of high pollution
Get up and move around for a few minutes every hour
Adjust ventilation and protection according to the actual environment
principles.remember: Variables outside the body are also counted in lifespan.

principles.title: Medications and supplements: Ask about the necessity first
principles.core: The more supplements, the better, let alone the medicines.
actions: Replenish when there are clear indications, such as confirmed vitamin D deficiency
Prescription drugs such as statins should be evaluated by doctors
Recheck indicators regularly, rather than adjusting based on feeling
principles.remember: Diagnosis first, then intervention.

principles.title: Sustainability is more important than intensity
principles.core: A moderate program that can last for ten years is better than an extreme program for three weeks.
actions: Start with the smallest executable action
Record and look back at your actual data
Allow adjustments and don’t pursue perfection
principles.remember: Live longer by repetition.

guides.name: Kitchen and Cooking
guides.desc: Replace "appropriate amount" with grams, and "a little" with a standard that can be judged.
guides.longDesc: Compiled from "HowToCook". It uses a unified template to constrain each dish: ingredients are calculated by portion, step numbers, waiting time or judgment criteria. The items here distill the methodology itself.

principles.title: Write the number of grams clearly and refuse "appropriate amount"
principles.core: The vagueness of the recipe is the starting point for the kitchen to overturn.
actions: The raw materials are given in grams or milliliters according to the portion
The heat and time are judged as standards
The range of empirical seasonings is written, and the taste differences are noted
principles.remember: If you can weigh it, don't rely on feeling.

principles.title: Prepare the ingredients first, then start the fire
principles.core: Being in a hurry is probably because it was not prepared in advance.
actions: Prepare the ingredients and tools according to the recipe
Arrange the processing sequence according to the time required
Mark the error-prone steps separately
principles.remember: Prepare the ingredients in place and cook without panic.

principles.title: There are basic rules for removing fishy smell and heating
principles.core: Most problems in the kitchen can be attributed to temperature and moisture.
actions: Blanch or pickle the meat according to the recommended method to remove the fishy smell
Distinguish the applicable ingredients for steaming, boiling, stir-frying, and frying
Wait for the time given in the step or clear judgment criteria
principles.remember: Control the fire, and control half of it.

principles.title: Food safety cannot depend on luck
principles.core: Just because the taste is not bad, it does not mean it is edible.
actions: Separate raw and cooked food
The storage temperature and duration are given according to the ingredients
Discard the ingredients that you are not sure about
principles.remember: If you are not sure, throw them away.

principles.title: The difficulty and calories are written into the recipe
principles.core: Before choosing a dish, look at the difficulty and cost.
actions: Give each dish a difficulty star rating and estimated time
Mark the main nutritional ingredients
Start with low-difficulty, high-frequency dishes
principles.remember: It is more important to make it well than to make it amazing.

principles.title: Check the tool list in advance
principles.core: If one tool is missing, the entire dish may come to a standstill.
actions: List the necessary tools before starting
Distinguish between necessary and optional
Newbies must first prepare the basic tools
principles.remember: If you want to do your job well, you must first list the tools.

guides.name: Introduction to Investment
guides.desc: Does not give the answer to "what to buy", but only teaches concepts, risk boundaries and check items before placing an order.
guides.longDesc: Compiled from "investing-for-beginners". It uses a word library to cover US stocks, options and cryptocurrencies, emphasizing risk boundaries and interest disclosure. The items here are extracted in a unified format of "Concept → Risk → Check Items".

principles.title: Understand the concept first, then place an order
principles.core: The most expensive tuition fee with zero foundation is to buy it if you don’t understand it.
actions: Start by reading basic terms before and after the market, order types, financial report valuations, etc.
Understand the trading mechanism before touching derivatives
Use the glossary to check back at any time, don't rely on memory
principles.remember: Don't press the code you can't understand.

principles.title: The risk boundary is written first
principles.core: First calculate the maximum loss, and then think about how much you can earn.
actions: Clear the maximum loss, position and exit conditions before placing an order
The upper limit of option losses can be roughly calculated based on "Price Difference × Quantity"
No need to participate with funds necessary for daily life
principles.remember: Think of losing first, then making profit.

principles.title: Leverage and Liquidation: Don’t regard luck as ability
principles.core: Leverage magnifies fluctuations, not winning rate.
actions: Understand the margin, liquidation and margin call mechanisms
Crypto contracts pay special attention to high volatility and high leverage combinations
Set the maximum tolerable drawdown and strictly implement it
principles.remember: It only takes one time to liquidate your position.

principles.title: Private keys and authorization: the bottom line of asset security
principles.core: On the chain, if you lose your private key, no one can help you retrieve it.
actions: Save the mnemonic phrase offline and never take screenshots or send it to others
Check the contract address and limit before authorization
Revoke unnecessary authorizations regularly
principles.remember: If it is not your private key, it is not your currency.

principles.title: Be wary of placing orders and "guaranteed profits"
principles.core: People who can really make guaranteed profits will not make money by recruiting you into a group.
actions: Remain suspicious of income promises and "inside information" by default
Do not open an account and deposit funds through private message links
Stop adding immediately if withdrawals are blocked
principles.remember: Promise of income is a risk signal.

principles.title: See clearly the benefits behind recommendations
principles.core: There may be rebates hidden in the recommendations.
actions: Read the commission statement of the platform comparison table
Distinguish between factual descriptions and sales pitches
Choose tools based on your own needs, not by ranking
principles.remember: See who is recommending first, and then what is recommended.

guides.name: Love and Relationships
guides.desc: Emotions are settled first, then facts are broken down, and finally an executable next step is given.
guides.longDesc: Compiled from "The Dog-Headed Military Advisor's Guide to Love". It turns interdisciplinary knowledge into situational decision-making workflows and makes it clear that consent, exit rights and safety boundaries cannot be bypassed. Entries here retain their Judgment → Action → Observation Window structure.

principles.title: Catch the person first, then deal with things
principles.core: When the emotions are not on the ground, any analysis is just noise.
actions: Acknowledge the other person’s feelings first and don’t rush to judge
Write facts, speculations, and unknowns separately
Wait until the mood is stable before discussing plans
principles.remember: Only when people are heard first can the conversation continue.

principles.title: Behaviors are more reliable than labels
principles.core: Look at what a person does, not who he says he is.
actions: Consistency and repeatability of observed behavior
Do not cover all behaviors with one label
Allow sufficient time window for observation
principles.remember: Listen to what they say, but also watch what they do.

principles.title: Consent and right to withdraw cannot be bypassed
principles.core: In any relationship, saying "no" must be safe and effective.
actions: Clarify your boundaries and bottom line
Respect the other party's rejection and withdrawal
Be wary of pressure, guilt kidnapping and isolation
principles.remember: Unwillingness is enough reason.

principles.title: Judge benefits: reciprocity, opportunity cost, safety
principles.core: A good relationship should make both parties better.
actions: See if the investment is roughly equal
Calculate what you have given up for this relationship
Take the sense of security as a hard indicator, not a bonus
principles.remember: Relationships also need to settle accounts, and the calculation is long-term.

principles.title: Words are the skeleton, not lines
principles.core: It is better to express your own meaning clearly than to copy love words.
actions: Use "Feelings + Facts + Requests" to organize expressions
Prepare observation windows and stopping conditions
Look back at the other party's true reaction after speaking
principles.remember: Sincerity requires structure, not routines.

principles.title: Breakup and reconciliation: look at changes, not commitments
principles.core: The prerequisite for reconciliation is that the problem is really solved.
actions: Make clear the reasons for separation and the unacceptable items
Observe stable changes over a period of time
Ask a trusted third party if necessary
principles.remember: Reuniting is a new choice, not a return to the past.

principles.title: The strength of evidence must be graded
principles.core: Psychological conclusions also have applicable conditions.
actions: Distinguish between research conclusions, empirical suggestions and personal opinions
Do not regard a single theory as a master key
Remain ethically vigilant about manipulation techniques
principles.remember: Methods are useful, but boundaries are more important.

guides.name: Life Advancement
guides.desc: Recovery manual after failure, unemployment, and trough: write down the problem and complete a visible action.
guides.longDesc: Organized from "byoungd/up". It is not a successful learning, nor does it promise results, but a cycle of "write down the question → complete a visible action → retest and review". The entries here retain their restrained, small-step, repeatable expression.

principles.title: Put yourself back into life first
principles.core: The first step when you are at a trough is not to turn over, but to return to your daily routine.
actions: Reestablish the basic rhythm of eating, sleeping, and going out
Lower your goal to a small thing that can be accomplished today
Allow yourself to be slow
principles.remember: Live the daily routine first, and then talk about the future.

principles.title: Write down the problem instead of dwelling on
principles.core: the vague anxiety. Write it down and it becomes a manageable problem.
actions: Write down the current biggest problem in one sentence
List the known, unknown and verifiable things in the next step
Decompose the big problem into visible actions
principles.remember: Half of the problem written out has been solved.

principles.title: Complete a visible action
principles.core: Recovery relies on action, not epiphany.
actions: Do a small thing that can be seen every day
Record the completed fact, not the current feeling
Start from the smallest unit and accumulate
principles.remember: Do one thing, count it as one.

principles.title: Use Tools to Amplify Your Abilities
principles.core: Don’t rely on your status, let the tools save you effort.
actions: Hand over repetitive work to checklists, templates or software
Build a weekly review sheet
Use a 90-day action sheet to track long-term goals
principles.remember: Those who know how to use tools move faster.

principles.title: Retest periodically, do not pursue a straight rise
principles.core: Recovery is fluctuating, use cycles to see the trend.
actions: Review the status and completion level at a fixed time every week
Allow to go back and adjust the next goal
Write the review into a comparable record
principles.remember: Look at the trend, not a specific day.

principles.title: Make it clear who is suitable and who is not suitable
principles.core: Any method has its applicable boundaries.
actions: Determine which stage you are currently in
Do not regard other people's paths as the standard answer
Ask for professional help promptly
principles.remember: Recognize yourself first, and then choose a method.

principles.title: Getting along with yourself
principles.core: Long-term changes require ultimately coming to terms with one's own rhythm.
actions: Reduce self-competition comparison
Make a proper place for rest
Treat "good enough" as a sustainable standard
principles.remember: Side with yourself.

guides.name: Law & Rights
guides.desc: Basic rights and actions in employment, renting, consumer disputes, lending and family affairs.
guides.longDesc: Common legal issues by life scenario: keep evidence first, follow the process, and know what to fight for and what to avoid.

guides.name: Emergency & Safety
guides.desc: First response, common accidents, health emergencies and household preparedness.
guides.longDesc: Call for help first, protect yourself before helping others. Each entry is written as a memorable sequence of actions.

guides.name: Mind & Emotions
guides.desc: Recognizing emotions, daily regulation, low periods and seeking support.
guides.longDesc: Separate feelings, facts and thoughts; recover rhythm with small actions; recognize signs that professional help is needed.

guides.name: Focus & Tools
guides.desc: Lightweight methods for tasks, notes, tools and personal energy.
guides.longDesc: Fewer tool switches, more records; use lists to free attention and reviews instead of self-blame.

guides.name: Family & Care
guides.desc: Care basics, growth and education, household collaboration and safety preparation.
guides.longDesc: From infant care to elder support, make invisible household work and boundaries explicit.

guides.name: Travel & Mobility
guides.desc: Preparation, safety on the road, health emergencies and post-trip review.
guides.longDesc: Documents, valuables, payments and emergency contacts are the basics; leave room in the itinerary for surprises.

references.name: Guide to Preventing Fraud
references.desc: 405 real scams are dismantled, classified according to routines, losses, and victim groups, with verification records and emergency procedures attached.

references.name: Cost-effective life guide
references.desc: 772 pieces of advice with costs, benefits, and levels of evidence, covering health, money, law, and rock bottom situations.

references.desc: How to get along on campus and in the workplace, including key judgments, examples, effects and exceptions.

references.desc: Facing the recovery after failure and trough, use the "write down the problem - visible action - retest" cycle to advance.
